newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain six-mth bills seen at record low at auction.
newsitem.headline: Spain six-mth bills seen at record low at auction.

text.p: Spanish Treasury six-month bill yields should set a record low at an auction on Wednesday, after the previous sale at 6.042 percent on December 3, dealers said.
The bills were trading on the grey market on Tuesday morning at around 5.88/5.95 percent and the expectation was that they would be allotted at around 5.90 percent.
On December 13 the Bank of Spain cut its key money market rate by 50 basis points to 6.25 percent.
"Interbank rates have declined, especially after the official rate reduction and the lower-than-expected CPI," a dealer said.
November CPI was unchanged on the month to give a 3.2 percent year-on-year rise from 3.5 percent in October.
"Tomorrow bill yields could go below six percent even though there's not much demand" another added.
A week ago, the one-year bill auction set a record low at 5.90 percent.
